edits.reason: The client distinguishes enjoyed vacation (79001), paid leave (79018) and vacation compensated in cash (79003). The first two map to X and L as the spec says. 79003 is a cash payment with no time off (two rows have no end date and start months before the period), and the spec does not say whether it raises VAC-LR. Without that rule a developer mapping 'all vacation WTs' would flag VAC-LR with dates outside the period.

edits.current: Tipo de salario. X = salario integral; F = salario fijo; V = salario variable. Where X, the contribution base is 70% of the integral salary, not 100%, because 30% is the statutory prestacional factor (CST art. 132 num. 2, minimum 13 SMMLV). Maps to electronic payroll SalarioIntegral (NIE056) for the X case. Source: AT2 v30 (MinSalud, Res. 2388/2016 Anexo Técnico 2, version 30, 24-07-2026) §2.1.2.1 campo 41 and §2.1.2.3.40.
edits.proposed: Tipo de salario. X = salario integral; F = salario fijo; V = salario variable. Where X, the contribution base is 70% of the integral salary, not 100%, because 30% is the statutory prestacional factor (CST art. 132 num. 2, minimum 13 SMMLV). Maps to electronic payroll SalarioIntegral (NIE056) for the X case. Source: AT2 v30 (MinSalud, Res. 2388/2016 Anexo Técnico 2, version 30, 24-07-2026) §2.1.2.1 campo 41 and §2.1.2.3.40. PMI source: no salary-type field in Master Data; X where the employee is paid WT 62140 Integral Salary in the period, F where paid WT 62100 Ordinary Salary; the rule for V must be confirmed. Where X, the 70% applies to the parafiscal base T2R2-095 as well as to the four IBC fields (CST art. 132; client WT 64991 = 70% of the integral salary).
edits.reason: Master Data has no salary-type field; integral employees are identifiable only by WT 62140. The client applies the 70% to the parafiscal base as well (64991 = 70% of the integral salary), while the spec condition only mentions the four IBC fields. The client also adds the Ley 1393 excess at 100% on top of the 70% (see T2R2-042).

edits.current: Contribution base for pension. FLOOR 1 SMMLV = COP 1,750,905; CEILING 25 SMMLV = COP 43,772,625 in 2026. Must reconcile to electronic payroll NIE166 divided by the rate in T2R2-046, allowing for the different rounding conventions. Bidirectional set with 'All-inclusive salary flag' (T2R2-041), which where marked sets this base to 70% of the all-inclusive salary, and with 'Solidarity pension fund - solidarity sub-account' (T2R2-051), which is payable only where this base reaches 4 SMMLV.
edits.proposed: Contribution base for pension. FLOOR 1 SMMLV = COP 1,750,905; CEILING 25 SMMLV = COP 43,772,625 in 2026. Must reconcile to electronic payroll NIE166 divided by the rate in T2R2-046, allowing for the different rounding conventions. Bidirectional set with 'All-inclusive salary flag' (T2R2-041), which where marked sets this base to 70% of the all-inclusive salary, and with 'Solidarity pension fund - solidarity sub-account' (T2R2-051), which is payable only where this base reaches 4 SMMLV. Computation order evidenced in the client data: (a) salary-constituting pay of the period (70% of it for an integral salary); (b) plus the excess of non-salary payments over 40% of TOTAL remuneration, the test being run on the full (100%) integral salary and the excess added at 100% (Ley 1393 de 2010 art. 30); (c) floor 1 SMMLV, ceiling 25 SMMLV; (d) round UP to the whole peso (the payroll intermediate value may carry decimals, e.g. 17300699.5). PMI reference values: Detail IBC per Employees S.S. 'IBC Total'; G2N WT 64995 'Non-SSI excess' holds the Ley 1393 add-back.
edits.reason: The client confirms the floor/ceiling, the 70% integral rule and the Ley 1393 40% clamp, and stores the add-back as its own WT (64995 'Non-SSI excess'). Two points the explanation does not tell the developer: (1) for an integral employee the 40% test is run on the FULL integral salary and the excess is added at 100% on top of the 70% base (employee 53618643: 0.7 x 22,761,765 + 5,175,959 = 21,109,194.3); (2) the client report carries unrounded bases with decimals (85 of 262 rows, e.g. 17300699.5) - the PILA base must be rounded UP to the whole peso. The client uses one base ('IBC Total') for pension, health and ARL.

edits.proposed: THE FIFTH AND MOST-MISSED BASE: IBC otros parafiscales diferentes a CCF - the base for SENA, ICBF, ESAP and MEN. Ley 21 de 1982 art. 17 defines it differently from the contribution bases: it includes paid rest days and it is UNCAPPED - the 25-SMMLV ceiling does not apply. Header campo T2R1-020 is the sum of campo 45 (IBC CCF), NOT of this field. Source: AT2 v30 (MinSalud, Res. 2388/2016 Anexo Técnico 2, version 30, 24-07-2026) campo 95. For an all-inclusive (integral) salary this base is 70% of the integral salary, like the IBC fields (CST art. 132). PMI reference: G2N WT 64991 'Parafiscals Base actual' (uncapped, includes paid vacation WT 79401).
edits.reason: Client data confirms the parafiscal base is uncapped and includes paid vacation (WT 79401), and that SENA 2% / ICBF 3% are computed on it. Missing from the explanation: for an integral salary the parafiscal base is also 70% (client 64991 = 17,300,699 for a 24,715,285 integral salary), and the client's CCF is computed on this base too (see Conflict on T2R2-045).

edits.current: 16% of the pension IBC - the WHOLE contribution, employer and employee together. The electronic payroll reports only the employee's 4% (NIE166); this field reports 16%. They are not interchangeable.
edits.proposed: 16% of the pension IBC - the WHOLE contribution, employer and employee together. The electronic payroll reports only the employee's 4% (NIE166); this field reports 16%. They are not interchangeable. Compute the PILA value as base x rate rounded UP to the next multiple of 100; do not copy the payroll wage-type amounts, which the client rounds to the peso (only 12 of 241 amounts are multiples of 100). PMI wage types for reconciliation: 2556 Pension Plan Mandatory - AFP Employee + 2567 Pension Plan Mandatory - AFP Employer.
edits.reason: Client splits the contribution into employee (WT 2556) and employer (WT 2567) wage types, rounded to the peso (12 of 241 employee amounts are multiples of 100). The explanation does not tell the developer to recompute and round to 100 rather than sum the payroll amounts.

edits.current: Voluntary contribution made BY THE EMPLOYEE into the mandatory pension fund.
edits.proposed: Voluntary contribution made BY THE EMPLOYEE into the mandatory pension fund. Do not map voluntary-pension-fund savings (for PMI the 'FVOL' wage types 25812-25823) to this field: they are paid to a voluntary fund, not to the mandatory pension fund, even where the administrator is the same company.
edits.reason: The client deducts voluntary pension savings to voluntary funds ('FVOL', WT 25812-25823), some run by the same administrators as the mandatory fund (Proteccion, Colfondos). These are not, on the evidence, voluntary contributions INTO the mandatory fund; without a warning a developer could map them here.

edits.current: 0.5% of the contribution base - 50% of the additional 1% (Ley 100 art. 27 num. 1 lit. a, as amended by Ley 797 de 2003 art. 8). Borne ENTIRELY BY THE EMPLOYEE and additional to the 4% pension. Reconciles to electronic payroll NIE168. Under AT2 v30 this value is LIQUIDATED BY THE INFORMATION OPERADOR according to the rules that apply to the contributor ('Lo liquida el Operador de Información'); the engine computes it for reconciliation and for the employee deduction, not as an input the operador accepts blindly.

edits.reason: The client's FSP rates match the spec's band table exactly, but the client carries solidarity and subsistence as ONE wage type (2553). The spec requires two separate fields; the developer must be told to split the combined amount, not map the WT to one field.

edits.current: Authorisation number issued by the EPS for the sick-leave benefit. Fifteen alphanumeric positions. Without it the EPS will not reimburse the employer's advance.
edits.proposed: Must be reported BLANK in every case under AT2 v30 ('Debe reportarse en blanco'). Incapacity and leave authorisations are no longer carried in PILA; EPS recovery runs outside this file. Do not map the incapacity/leave data of the payroll (for PMI, Leave Absence WTs 79006, 79008, 79011) to this field. Note: the 'Population Rules' sheet still instructs reporting these values and must be aligned.
edits.reason: The Field Explanation describes an authorisation number to be reported and says 'Without it the EPS will not reimburse', while the Conditional Reason says the field must be BLANK in every case under AT2 v30; the spec's Population Rules sheet also tells the engine to report these numbers. The client's Leave Absence report carries incapacity/maternity amounts, which invites a developer to map them. The explanation must state the blank rule unambiguously.

edits.current: Money value of the general-illness incapacity in the period. The employer ADVANCES it and recovers from the EPS - see the inbound EPS/ARL determination in the Report Matrix.
edits.proposed: Must be reported as ZERO in every case under AT2 v30 ('Debe reportarse en cero'). The benefit value advanced by the employer is recovered from the EPS outside this file. Note: the 'Population Rules' sheet still instructs reporting these values and must be aligned.
edits.reason: The Field Explanation describes the money value of the benefit, while the Conditional Reason says ZERO in every case under AT2 v30; the Population Rules sheet says report the values. The client's Leave Absence 'Amount' column holds exactly these values and must not be mapped here.

edits.current: Risk class of the work centre, reported as 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 (= Class I, II, III, IV, V). Bidirectional with 'Work centre' (T2R2-062): the class follows the work centre, so a VCT event can change it mid-period. Blank where the contributor is not obliged to contribute to occupational risk; for type 57 the class follows Decreto 1563 de 2016; for type 70 it is always 1. Source: AT2 v30 (MinSalud, Res. 2388/2016 Anexo Técnico 2, version 30, 24-07-2026) campo 78.
edits.proposed: Risk class of the work centre, reported as 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 (= Class I, II, III, IV, V). Bidirectional with 'Work centre' (T2R2-062): the class follows the work centre, so a VCT event can change it mid-period. Blank where the contributor is not obliged to contribute to occupational risk; for type 57 the class follows Decreto 1563 de 2016; for type 70 it is always 1. Source: AT2 v30 (MinSalud, Res. 2388/2016 Anexo Técnico 2, version 30, 24-07-2026) campo 78. PMI source: Master Data 'Employee Professional Risk Class (ARL)' is held per EMPLOYEE with mixed formats ('Class 1', '1'); normalise to the single digit 1-5. Because the class varies by employee/work centre, it cannot be sourced from a single company-level value.
edits.reason: Client stores the class as mixed text ('Class 1', 'Class 2') and digits ('1'); the field is A(1) with values 1-5. 5 employees have no class. The class is also held PER EMPLOYEE, while the System Mapping points to Company.Risk_Class, which cannot represent two classes (I and II) inside one company.
